cards.explanation: The answer is Christ. Paul says he promised them to one husband, “…to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.” Notice it's ONE husband, friends, not a lineup. I think Paul sounds like a man who takes a promise very seriously.

The answer is Eve. Paul says, “…just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning…” Back in the garden, when asked what she'd done, she said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.” (Genesis 3:13) Paul uses her story as a warning for the Corinthians, and I think that's a heavy thing to carry around.

The answer is True. Paul says, “I am afraid, however…” and then names the danger: that their minds “…may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.” He isn't telling them it's already happened. He's telling them what worries him, and a worry like that tells me he cares a lot.

The answer is that they put up with it very easily. If someone proclaims another Jesus, a different spirit or a different gospel, Paul says, “…you put up with it very easily.” Notice he says easily, friends. I think that word is what worries him.

The answer is in no way inferior. Paul says he's “…in no way inferior…” to those super-apostles, and that's from his own mouth in verse 5. Notice he's not saying he's better, just that he doesn't come up short. It's like being told you can't sit at the cool table, and you calmly say, “I'm fine right here.”

The answer is False. Paul says, “Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge.” He owns one thing and stands firm on the other. He even tells them, “We have made this clear to you in every way possible.”

The answer is that he preached the gospel free of charge. Paul asks if it was a sin “…because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?” He calls that humbling himself so he could exalt them. Think about that question, friends. He's asking whether it was a sin to charge nothing.

The answer is False. Paul says, “…the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs.” The Corinthians didn't carry that load, and Paul says he wasn't a burden to anyone there. Somebody else showed up when he needed it, and that's a good friend to have.

The answer is that he won't be a burden to them. Paul says, “I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.” Notice the two halves: what he did, and what he will keep doing. He's making a promise here, friends, and he doesn't hedge it.

The answer is True. Paul asks, “Why? Because I do not love you?” and then he answers right away: “God knows I do!” He calls on God as the One who knows his heart. He asks it and answers it in the same breath, friends.

The answer is to undercut men who want to seem his equals. Paul says he'll keep on, “…in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.” So his free-of-charge preaching has a purpose. It's aimed at those men's opportunity to be regarded as equals.
The answer is false. Paul says, “For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.” That's a direct word from him. He doesn't dance around it, friends.

The answer is Satan. Paul says, “…Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.” He uses that to say it's no wonder when others put on a disguise too. Then he adds in verse 15 that it isn't surprising if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness.
The answer is False. Paul says, “Their end will correspond to their actions.” These men put on a disguise, but verse 15 says their end matches what they did. The costume doesn't change that.
